(a) Construct a complete transcription unit with promoter and terminator on the basis of the hypothetical coding strand given below :
A T G C A T G C A T A G

questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE: the twelve bases A T G C A T G C A T A G printed above a horizontal line with a tick under each base and an arrowhead at BOTH ends. No 5' or 3' end is marked anywhere, which is why the scheme accepts either polarity. The bases are carried in the stem. Page idx 12.
questions._drawFigure: a double-stranded transcription unit: the coding strand ATGCATGCATAG and its complementary template strand TACGTACGTATC, both ends of each strand marked 5' and 3', with the promoter boxed at the 5' end of the coding strand (upstream) and the terminator at its 3' end (downstream), and the coding and template strands labelled.
questions._cbseVoided: The scheme prints two complete answers separated by '//': the coding strand read 5' to 3' left to right (promoter on the left, RNA 5'AUGCAUGCAUAG3') OR read 3' to 5' left to right (promoter on the right, RNA 5'GAUACGUACGUA3'), with the same mark split on each. Either is accepted because the printed strand marks no polarity.
questions._flag: The printed coding strand carries no 5'/3' labels, so the question has two correct answers; the scheme accepts both. The solution ships the 5' to 3' left-to-right reading and names the other.

questions.context: Immunity in our body is of two types (i) Innate immunity, and (ii) Acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas Acquired immunity is pathogen specific. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are four types of antibodies produced in our body — IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response where it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same antigen/pathogen. These immune responses are carried out with the help of two special types of lymphocytes present in the blood.
questions.stem: Name the two types of specialised cells which carry out the primary and secondary responses.
